item.title: Comment on Deep Research considers the costs and benefits of US AID by Stellar Mike
item.description:
"I would get rid of virtually all of the consultants, and make direct transfers to worthy African and Ukraine programs, thus lowering overhead. If such worthy programs exist, why not give them money directly? Are they so hard to find?"

I work in this sector, though not with USAID. Direct transfers to local entities is the industry vision ("localization", "decolonization") but the compliance burdens associated with receiving donor funding is enormous, hence an ongoing role for intermediaries. Even if these compliance burdens were erased, technical, managerial and financial capability is also generally low. Most good organizations would struggle with giant infusions of cash and the argument of intermediaries is that this would produce leakage into nefarious sphere (money siphoned to terrorists).

Not saying it can't be done better, but it's not an easy fix.
